record_notes.DCP-LETT-1898: June 10, 1856; all nine body blocks, five notes, annotations and bibliography independently read. Excluded salute-class node is actually the dateline June 10th/56, not a greeting. Replies to missing June 7 Darwin letter. Atlantic mild-humid climate argument rejects easy continental-land reasoning; northern connection hypothesized, and Ural submergence comparison is expressly a surmise not investigated. P3–6 are a three-column diagram flattened into literal diag/ramme prose; raw markup contains no table, MathML or actual image. P7 interprets columns 1/3 and islands 2, retain ordering without inventing restored layout. This distinctive comparison is the antecedent of 1899. Accusation about Forbes conscience is Watson opinion, not an established biographical fact. Darwin sequence number and other marks undated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1899: After June 10, 1856; full three retained blocks and four notes/bibliography read. ALS possibly incomplete and damaged; starts And now, so do not recreate opening. XML June 11–30 is broad editorial range. Full June 20 answer 1907 supplies an inclusive upper relational bound June 20, not June 19 since same-day composition/receipt is not independently excluded. P1 explicitly acknowledges 1898 Europe/East Asia submerged-land comparison and asks Arctic-circle distribution with Scandinavia/Gulf Stream qualification. Hypothesis warmer mid-Pliocene, nearly continuous 65–75 degree land, southward glacial movement and partial northward return is tentative, not established observation. Later Natural selection/Origin exposition remains editorial future context.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1907: June 20, 1856; all twelve blocks, six notes, separate annotations and bibliography freshly reread, in addition to prior accepted batch07 reading. 1835 list now outdated but broad northward-distribution claim retained. Syme quoted in P3–4, not Watson own original observation; first agrarian-variation question belongs to earlier missing prompt, while P1/P4/P6–9 directly answer 1899 northern-sharing question. Twenty-two candidate exceptions, some five or six possibly transported, group categories not necessarily disjoint; E Asia/W America comparison data inadequate. Proposed Spain/Ireland promontories or volcanic islands and climatic tolerances are hypothetical, no historical route proved. Darwin numbered series and brown marks undated. Prior 1944 witness at August24 remains valid later knowledge evidence and is not recounted here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1985: November 10, 1856; all nine blocks, two notes, separate annotations and bibliography read. Opening explicitly responds to published sea-water germination experiments, paper read May6, not private 1978 Fox letter. Acknowledges months of seed resistance; challenges extrapolation from sinking plants in still shallow water to moving seas. Agitation delaying decay and seaweed entanglement are possibilities/questions, not demonstrated dispersal. Mud analogy distinct from seed experiment. Undated Darwin Limosella and hawk/bird-feet/root-earth marks cannot establish receipt date or provide a missing Darwin reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1994: November19, 1856 damaged ALS; all thirty retained blocks, four notes, annotations and bibliography read. Responds to a missing Darwin letter, probably answering 1985, not to 1899. Embedded-root seeds germination near-certain individual recollection; navigation possibility/probability qualified. Still-water clarification refers to published page135 plant-decay reasoning, not seed germinating power. Fourth London Catalogue keeps first-edition numbers plus starred insertions:1428+132=1560 minus17=1543 actual names; roughly200 ambiguous among them,36 Rubus, total over1800 with over450 alternatively varieties. Tables/list fragments are literal flattened diag/ramme and hypothetical timeline includes raw1111 repeats; no images/MathML/table structure, do not silently replace repeats with dates. Ranunculus split examples and fictitious 1700–1856 chronology show classification instability, not dated evolutionary events. All used note and crossings undated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2002: November26, 1856; all seven blocks, four notes and bibliography read. Answers missing Subularia/Limosella flowering query, not June Arctic-circle letter1899. Subularia memory decades old explicitly unreliable and specimens in bud, does not meet query; quotes Koch Latin about submerged and emerged flowering separately from observation. Limosella personal observations show flowering out of water and after rain submergence, not uninterrupted underwater bud development. 1843 watering-can transport is a probable explanation, not directly observed seed carriage. Dickie suggested as possible source; later Dickie answer is a separate record.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2023: Memorandum with date December28,1856 supplied from explicit Darwin annotation. Full43 blocks, two notes including entire extensive modern taxonomic gloss, annotations and bibliography read. Fourteen opening common/rare taxon pairs in P2–15, raw duplicate Gentiana germanica authorities and Asplenium negriem spelling retained. Three distinct intermediate-form categories: series bridging species; both species approximate; one varies toward other without reaching it. Eleven detailed examples plus compact final list with twelve named groups include Potentilla and Juncus additional entries. Prose category uncertainty and hybrid interpretations preserved, not proof all taxa are one species. Flattened diag/ramme list mapping must remain source-bound; no image/table/MathML. Dated Darwin heading supports knowledge by December28, not exact receipt or certain Watson writing day; remaining Q/12 marks undated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2106: June14, supplied1857; all three body blocks, four notes, complete separate enclosure and bibliography read. Watson sends extract supporting his earlier answer2002 to Darwin missing question; same-author follow-up is not a Darwin answer or reverse reply to2002. Enclosure quotes Graham report read February9,1843 concerning August1842 excursion after remarkably dry season, with Subularia and Lobelia flowering/fruiting on dry ground. Those are source-event dates, not Darwin knowledge dates; no demonstrated receipt or later use (editorial note says not used in specified discussion).
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2183: December14, supplied1857; all nine blocks, four notes, annotations and bibliography read. Promises return annotated British varieties list in few days, not completed return. Commingling often unknown from garden/herbarium material or forgotten collection context. Site-dependent forms and selection bias explicit: known situation varieties excluded from desired list, illustrated Polygonum amphibium alpha natans/beta terrestre flattened across P4–5. Geographic type/variety ranges qualified, alpine exception overlaps. Wants1857 Catalogue but Darwin used1853 list; spring printing planned, publication1859 only future apparatus. List DAR45:9–15 described, not fully transcribed. Undated All used/heading separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2190: December20, supplied1857; all four blocks, four notes and bibliography read. Returns to same missing varieties-list request as2183; repeatedly attempted but cannot supply concise item-by-item judgments, believes annotations spoiled list. Species definitions and unequal rank units frustrate comparison/generalisations. His inability to prove definite immutable species is qualified epistemic claim, not proof all species mutable. Preparing final Cybele volume not already published. Annotated list archived, not reproduced; no Darwin response survives in this packet.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1891: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Watson June 5, 1856, nine retained blocks including complete long six-taxon appended list, annotations, all notes and bibliography read. Recasts missing Darwin letter as four questions. Supports earlier publication but no publication completed. Describes three forms of geography work and unpublished 39-species fragment; old table incomplete/outdated. Northern absence exceptions hinge identity/nativity. Agrarian 40–50 strict and similar broader group, no greater average variability, two strong Polygonum/Viola exceptions and annual/perennial hypothesis. Full list Chrysosplenium/Isnardia/Astragalus/Thlaspi/Arenaria/Lythrum has cautious taxonomy, introductions and range qualifications; exact six reused in 1944 P3. Do not upgrade doubtful species identity or force categorical zero exceptions. Darwin notes undated; laterreplacement by Gray apparatus not contemporary. Available by August 24 witness, possible earlier Watson response pending packet 20.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2063: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional incomplete Watson March 10, 1857 source fully read: five retained blocks, salutation, annotations, footnotes and bibliography. Defines three alternative meanings of variable genera with Carex/Ranunculus, Rubus/Hieracium and Viola/Saxifraga examples. Distinguishes close stable species from inseparable variable complexes. Thinks Gray may mean first while Darwin means second or third, but text ends mid-sentence after copy proposal; no missing continuation invented. Raw yes certainly has no separate-hand markup, so no attribution silently changed. Darwin Please return and 1) annotations separately support forwarded note identification; March 16–31 outgoing 2060 explicitly forwards numbered note and asks Gray about this precise distinction. Companion Watson-to-Gray essay 2065 awaits supplemental admission.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1978: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October 20, supplied 1856; all nine blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Missing Fox answers include family/school and health, not a surviving pea case. Eagle/owl seed pellets regurgitated after eighteen and sixteen hours with seeds apparently intact; germination still under test. Experimental-book quote in footnote has true sixteen and a quarter MathML hours and is a separate witness, not silent replacement of rounded body sixteen. Asks nephew to test lizard/snake eggs floating five or ten days; not experiment completed. December 19 pea material addresses public legume query, not this request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1750: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Supplied August 26, 1855 based on October 2 Watson reply. Surviving source is Darwin signed draft, not proven verbatim final sent copy. Explicitly answers August 23 numerical figure, structural comparability of genera, British flora as fragment, and expected variable-character example. Reports Gray averages 6.37 versus 4.67 and source-stated excess 1.7, compared with Watson 1.68; mathematically decimal subtraction may yield 1.70, but preserve author notation. P7 explains why he concealed the objective and now regrets it. October reply proves corresponding letter of August 26 was received by Watson, without dating dispatch/receipt precisely or proving every draft word sent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1758: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October 2, 1855. Explicitly replies after delay to Darwin August 26 and quotes existing fauna/flora as mere fragment, uniquely matching draft 1750. Challenges local versus global genus sizes, distinguishes breadth of extremes from density of intermediates and number of diagnostic comparisons, then critiques inconsistent species and reproductive-organ genus classification. All seventeen body blocks and textual numerical/plant comparisons read. Separate Darwin annotations and full keyed note on reproductive organs are undated; do not treat them as Watson text or known October 2. Counterexamples and personal convictions remain qualified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1764: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October 11, 1855. Sends a second marked catalogue separately from covering sheet, extending debateable forms with Babington/Newman varieties and distinguishing species-like varieties from well-defined close pairs. Gives local-versus-global comparison argument, comments on an unlocated Darwin letter mentioning Forbes, and makes Watson own accusations against Forbes. Those accusations are attributed opinion, not narrator findings. Ranunculus leaf table and hypothetical Saxifraga Andrewsii case answer or seek clarification of variable-character rule; specimen not examined, inference from description/figure only. Same-author October 2 source 1758 is not an incoming Darwin prompt. Later Darwin annotations, including yes-this-is-case, have no date here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1775: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 8, 1855. Watson remains interested but considers statistics weaker indications than Darwin does, because taxonomic groups and species judgments vary. Recommends combining 69, 195 and 32 into 296 debateable forms, with plus/equal/minus denoting probable species, possible species and probable varieties. Polygonum example distinguishes catalogue omission from biological absence of variation; hypothetical imported forms are not actual introductions. Expresses his own bias toward species not immutably distinct. Responds within ongoing correspondence but no uniquely identified surviving Darwin prompt; annotations are undated.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
